queries.text: For the Yang-Mills matrix-model (Yang-Mills quantum mechanics) potential built from squared cross products of several R^3 vectors, why is the sum of squared gradients of the commutator (cross-product) components exactly a constant times the sum of the squared vector lengths, even along the flat directions (collinear, commuting configurations) where the gradient of the potential vanishes, and what are the stiffness (squared frequency) and degeneracy of the transverse oscillator modes there?

Quartic cross-product potential V = sum |A_i x A_j|^2 for several three-vectors: at aligned (valley, zero-mode) configurations the potential gradient vanishes but the total squared derivative of the cross-product components is a fixed multiple of the summed squared lengths; what is the transverse normal-mode stiffness and multiplicity at such points?

Flat directions of a squared-commutator potential for several three-vectors: identity that the total squared derivative of the commutator components is proportional to the summed squared lengths at collinear configurations, and the stiffness and multiplicity of the transverse harmonic modes (the mechanism behind a discrete spectrum despite non-compact flat directions).

Coupled three-vectors with squared cross product interaction: total squared derivative of the commutator components as a constant multiple of the summed squared lengths at aligned configurations with vanishing potential gradient; stiffness and degeneracy of the transverse normal modes.
